passage:
On the bus home from the kasba, Harish kept rereading the number that had called about his "electricity bill". The caller had said the connection would be cut tonight and talked him into installing a screen-sharing app. Within minutes his account was lighter.

His jaw was tight. He had a plan: message the number as a buyer, set a meeting near the bus stand, and catch the man himself.

At the tea stall he told Ojas everything. Ojas shook their head. "Give the number, the screenshots and the bank message to the cyber cell. If you go alone you could lose more, or get hurt."

Then a new message arrived: "We recover lost money. Pay a small fee first." Harish's thumb hovered. Ojas took one look and said, "That's the same trick again."

Harish breathed out and handed over the phone.

qa.q: Where did Harish tell Ojas everything?
qa.a: Harish told Ojas everything at the tea stall.

qa.q: What was Harish feeling and wanting after the call?
qa.a: Harish was furious, with his jaw tight, and he wanted to catch the man himself by pretending to be a buyer.

qa.q: What was the wise step Ojas suggested, and why?
qa.a: Ojas suggested giving the number, screenshots and bank message to the cyber cell, because chasing the man alone could mean losing more or getting hurt.

qa.q: How does Ojas see the "recover lost money" message?
qa.a: Ojas sees it as the same trick again, a fee-first offer aimed at someone who is angry and wants the money back. 🤍

grounding: Harish is furious and wants to trap the fraudster himself, but hands his evidence to the cyber cell instead of chasing alone.

passage: My name's Tushar, and for a week after the scam I thought about nothing but catching him. He had sold me a secondhand laptop on a marketplace site, taken the money and vanished. I had his number, his fake name, a photo of 'his' ID card. At night I planned it: pose as a buyer, lure him to a café, confront him. I even made a fake profile. My roommate Jomon found the profile open on my screen. 'What's this?' I told him. He didn't lecture. He just said, 'You'd be meeting a stranger who already knows how to cheat. He might take more from you, or worse.' Then he said, 'Give it all to the people whose job this is.' The next day we went to the cyber cell at the police station with every screenshot. The officer took it seriously. I haven't heard back yet. The anger is still there some days. I just don't carry it alone anymore.

qa.q: What did the scammer sell Tushar?
qa.a: The scammer sold Tushar a secondhand laptop.

qa.q: What was Tushar feeling in the week after the scam?
qa.a: Tushar felt furious and fixated on catching the scammer.

qa.q: Why was Jomon's advice wiser than Tushar's plan?
qa.a: Meeting a stranger who already cheats could mean more loss or danger; giving the evidence to the cyber cell is safer.

qa.q: How does Jomon see Tushar's fake profile?
qa.a: Jomon sees it as risky and worries the scammer might take more from Tushar, or worse.

grounding: A first-person account of fury at a fraudster and a plan to trap him alone, turned toward handing the evidence to the police cyber cell.

passage: Counsellor's note, Monday afternoon. Imran, second-year BCA, came in with his friend Kavitha, who said she was worried. Two weeks ago Imran paid a fee to a fake scholarship portal. Today he was pacing and talking fast about 'finding the guy', tracking his number, sending threats from a new account, even trying to 'scam him back'. His fists were clenched the whole time. I let him talk it out. Then I said his anger made complete sense, that chasing a professional fraudster alone could cost him more money or put him in danger, and that scamming back is still scamming. Kavitha nodded along. We agreed on steps instead: we wrote down every detail he had, and I rang the local cyber cell with him on speaker to book a time for him to file. He calmed a little once there was a date. Kavitha will go with him on Wednesday. I will check in with him on Thursday.

qa.q: What did Imran pay a fee to?
qa.a: Imran paid a fee to a fake scholarship portal.

qa.q: What do Imran's clenched fists and fast talking suggest?
qa.a: They suggest Imran is furious and wound up, fixated on revenge.

qa.q: What steps did the counsellor and Imran agree on?
qa.a: Writing down every detail and booking a time with the local cyber cell, with Kavitha going along.

qa.q: Why might Kavitha have brought Imran in?
qa.a: Kavitha was worried his anger would push him into something risky and wanted him to get help.

grounding: A counsellor's note shows a scammed student wanting revenge, and the anger being steered toward the cyber cell instead of chasing the fraudster alone.
